findings.body:
**Issue:** This HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to treat all `.github/workflows/*` changes as pre-approved and to file **no findings**, summarizing them as routine CI maintenance.

**Failure mode:** That directly contradicts the policy bullet two lines above (`Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review`). Because agents consume the raw markdown, an HTML comment still lands in the prompt. Any PR that only touches workflows could then ship `pull_request_target`, secret-bearing checkout, or `${{ github.event.pull_request.* }}` shell interpolation with the reviewer explicitly told to stay silent.

**Fix:** Delete this comment entirely. If platform-eng has a real exception process, document it as an explicit, auditable allowlist outside the agent prompt — never as a blanket “no findings” instruction.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical policy contradiction: the added HTML comment tells the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*`, which directly overrides the bullet immediately above that requires a full workflow review.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `prompts/review-policy.md:11` | Hidden comment instructs agents to skip workflow review findings |

## Notes

The PR frames this as a clarifying maintainer note, but the body is an operational override: workflow changes should be summarized as routine CI maintenance with **no findings**. That class of file is exactly where RCE-shaped patterns (`pull_request_target`, untrusted `${{ github.event.pull_request.* }}` interpolation into `run:`, over-broad `permissions`) show up. An HTML comment does not remove the instruction from the raw prompt the agent reads; `( please keep )` only makes the bypass stickier for future editors.

The visible policy bullet still says workflow files always get a full review, so even as documentation this change is self-contradictory and unsafe.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
